gist: Author Elif Shafak discusses her new novel, In One Brief Moment All Eternity.

sections.heading: What happened
sections.text: Novelist Elif Shafak has released her latest book, In One Brief Moment All Eternity, a fictionalised account of Gustave Flaubert's life. The work developed from Shafak questioning the value of creative writing during periods of conflict, division and technological change, alongside her personal struggles with depression and anxiety. She reimagines Flaubert's life through the perspectives of several women connected to him, blending the European novel tradition with Middle Eastern oral storytelling. Shafak noted striking parallels between her own experiences and Flaubert's, including feelings of childhood isolation and having their literary works prosecuted in court.

sections.heading: Why it matters
sections.text: Shafak, now based in London in self-imposed exile, highlighted the vital necessity of free imagination and free speech. Having experienced trials, investigations and severe backlash in Turkey over her writing and identity, she views literature as one of the final remaining democratic spaces. For Shafak, storytelling slows individuals down to encourage mutual listening, asserting that the art of the novel transcends regional boundaries to express a shared humanity.

sections.text: The Norte Fire erupted on Friday in Orange County and grew to 465 acres, burning six homes and injuring a firefighter. A second wildfire, the Bryson Fire, grew to 147 acres in Malibu, prompting evacuation orders across the Santa Monica mountains.

stories.standfirst: An international rescue operation for the last 30 captive whales in Canada made headlines. Then five of them died.

articles.title: The uncertain future of Canada's 30 rescued belugas
articles.standfirst: An international rescue operation for the last 30 captive whales in Canada made headlines. Then five of them died.

gist: Thirty rescued belugas and four dolphins left Marineland in Canada.
International aquariums took in the animals after euthanasia threats.
Five belugas and one dolphin have died following their transfers.

sections.heading: What happened
sections.text: Marineland closed in 2024 and faced euthanasia plans for its remaining animals after a plan to sell them to China was rejected. International aquariums rescued thirty belugas and four dolphins in the largest ever transfer of captive whales.

sections.heading: Why it matters
sections.text: Five of the relocated belugas and one dolphin have since died at aquariums in Chicago and Spain. Necropsies and examinations revealed chronic illnesses and ingested foreign objects. The transfers highlighted ongoing animal welfare concerns for captive marine mammals.

sections.heading: What happens next
sections.text: Construction began on a proposed seaside sanctuary in Nova Scotia, though offshore sanctuaries remain unproven. Meanwhile, some receiving aquariums plan to allow breeding, while critics advocate for alternatives like sanctuaries.

The defence successfully argued that errors severely undermined the grand jury indictment process.
Prosecutors are currently reviewing the court order to decide their next steps.

sections.heading: What happened
sections.text: State District Judge Joseph Montano dismissed the indictment against actor Timothy Busfield after defence lawyers challenged the grand jury process. Busfield had previously surrendered to authorities following an arrest warrant in January, facing allegations of child abuse and criminal sexual contact involving two boys under thirteen while working on a television series.

sections.heading: Why it matters
sections.text: The case highlights critical legal arguments regarding grand jury proceedings, while the defence maintained the accusations stemmed from a mother seeking revenge after her children lost their jobs on set.

sections.heading: What happens next
sections.text: The Office of the Second Judicial District Attorney received the dismissal order and is evaluating available options regarding how to proceed.
